title: Statistical Practice

gradingBreakdown.component: Short writing assignments (memos, 6-8 over the term)
Attendance and participation in class discussions
In-class handwritten writing exercise (blue book, no references)
Individual oral exams (15 min each, last five lab meetings)

weeklyTopics: ~6 case studies covering open-access datasets, each discussed for 2-3 weeks
Formulating compelling and tractable research questions
Assessing dataset structure, sampling, and measurement for research aims
Implementing statistical methods (including GLMs and newer methods) and conducting analysis
Assessing a priori potential outcomes/failure modes of an analysis, including statistical power
Communicating methods and findings to varied stakeholders, in writing and orally
Assigned readings from the statistics and broader scientific literature
In-class handwritten exam memo (October 28 per this offering)
Individual oral exams during the final five lab meetings (starting November 4 per this offering)
workloadNotes: PhD-level seminar for 2nd-year Statistics PhD students (prerequisite: STATS 600 and either 511 or 610); discussion-based, not lecture-based; heavy emphasis on oral defense of written work via individual 15-minute oral exams tailored to each student's own memos; code is not submitted for grading.
prerequisitesText: STATS 600 and either STATS 511 or STATS 610.
